# Combine Middleware ​

Combine Middleware combines multiple middleware functions into a single middleware. It provides three functions:

 `some` - Runs only one of the given middleware.
 `every` - Runs all given middleware.
 `except` - Runs all given middleware only if a condition is not met.

import { Hono } from 'hono' import { Hono } from  'hono'import { some, every, except } from 'hono/combine' import { some, every, except } from 'hono/combine'
```

## Global Response ​

Hono RPC client doesn't automatically infer response types from global error handlers like `app.onError()` or global middleware. You can use the `ApplyGlobalResponse` type helper to merge global error response types into all routes.

```

## Status code ​ [...] ts

```
if (res.ok) {if (res.ok) { const data = await res.json()  const  data =  await res. json() console.log(data.message) console. log(data.message)}}
```

### Cookies ​

To make the client send cookies with every request, add `{ 'init': { 'credentials": 'include' } }` to the options when you're creating the client.

## Description

[![@syfxlin](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/28844480?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/syfxlin)

[syfxlin](https://github.com/syfxlin)

opened [on May 15, 2024](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/2681#issue-2298304618)

### What version of Hono are you using?

4\.3.7

### What runtime/platform is your app running on?

Node.js

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When using `new Response` as a return value, the headers set by `c.header()` are lost in the actual response. If the response is returned using c.text, the headers will appear normally in the actual response.

[![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/28844480/330869655-f828b5a8-0d09-44ad-bf72-67b39b50fb3e.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..mHN2Omk0o4JPwdCA0Uzor1p0jXW11eYW95VBnXxSLJ8)](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/28844480/330869655-f828b5a8-0d09-44ad-bf72-67b39b50fb3e.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..mHN2Omk0o4JPwdCA0Uzor1p0jXW11eYW95VBnXxSLJ8)

1. Run `pnpm init`

2. Run `pnpm i hono @hono/node-server`

3. Paste the following code into the index.mjs file

```
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { setCookie } from "hono/cookie";

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/',async (c, next) => {
  setCookie(c, 'x-cookie-1', '1')
  c.header('x-test-1', '1')
  c.res.headers.set('x-test-2', '2')
  await next()
  setCookie(c, 'x-cookie-2', '2')
  c.header('x-test-3', '3')
  c.res.headers.set('x-test-4', '4')
}, async (c) => {
  setCookie(c, 'x-cookie-0', '0')
  c.header('x-test-0', '0')
  c.res.headers.set('x-test-0', '0')
  return new Response('Hello Node.js!')
  // return c.text('Hello Node.js!')
})

serve(app)
```

4. Run `node index.mjs`

5. Run `curl http://localhost:3000 -v`

### What is the expected behavior?

The actual response should contain all the set headers.

### What do you see instead?

> The following is my analysis, I just using Hono for less than half a month, so the analysis may not be accurate.

- When the header is set using `c.header` before creating the response, it is stored in `c.#header`, See: [https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/context.ts#L297](https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/context.ts#L297)

- If there is a return Response in the middleware, it will be set back to `c.res`, See: [https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/compose.ts#L60](https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/compose.ts#L60)

- The headers in `c.#res.headers` will then be copied into the response returned from the middleware (\_res), See: [https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/context.ts#L196-L212](https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/context.ts#L196-L212)

- But I don't see the c.#headers copying process, which could be the reason for the missing request headers.

### Additional information

*No response*

   Some say that a context header should be added to the `new Response()`. But, as [this comment](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/1526#issuecomment-1837052075), we don't want a design where header values are implicitly added to the Response object. If the user wants to add the header in context, they should use `c.body()`.

   Hi [@yusukebe](https://github.com/yusukebe), sometimes, we may not be able to return a response using `c.body` (which is often the case when using some third-party middleware), but need to set certain request headers before the handler, for example, setting a cookie before it reaches the [`authHandler`](https://github.com/honojs/middleware/blob/main/packages/auth-js/src/index.ts#L131) when using `@hono/auth-js` ([Auth.js database session \+ credentials](https://github.com/decovicdev/next-auth-database-session/blob/main/apps/app-dir-v4/app/api/auth/%5B...nextauth%5D/route.ts#L113)). Inconsistency in the behavior of `c.header` and `c.res.headers.set` can also confuse.

   ### yusukebe commented on May 16, 2024

   [![@yusukebe](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/10682?u=e25e17b3626c5ed31c5304a9539cff96dd36e7d1&v=4&size=48)](/yusukebe)

   [yusukebe](/yusukebe)

   [on May 16, 2024](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/2681#issuecomment-2114026871)

   Member

   The same issue was discussed in [\#1526](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/1526)

   Some say that a context header should be added to the `new Response()`. But, as [this comment](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/1526#issuecomment-1837052075), we don't want a design where header values are implicitly added to the Response object. If the user wants to add the header in context, they should use `c.body()`.

   Regarding `@hono/auth-js`, it should use `c.body()` instead of `new Response()`.

TASK: Fix the Set-Cookie merge bug in the `Context.res` setter in `src/context.ts` and add regression coverage in `src/context.test.ts`. Only these two files may change. Do NOT stage or commit anything; leave changes unstaged.

CURRENT BUG (src/context.ts lines ~414-434): when `this.#res` already exists and a new Response `_res` is assigned, the setter copies headers. For Set-Cookie it currently does:
  const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
  _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
  for (const cookie of cookies) _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
This deletes the incoming response's own Set-Cookie headers, so a cookie set by middleware on `c.res` causes the handler's raw `new Response(...)` Set-Cookie header(s) to be lost.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR:
1. When middleware has already set a cookie on `c.res` (e.g. `c.res.headers.append('set-cookie', 'middleware=1; Path=/')`, or `setCookie(c, ...)` before the response is materialized so it sits in `#preparedHeaders`) and the handler returns a new Response with its own Set-Cookie header, BOTH cookies must survive in the final `c.res`.
2. Preserve existing non-cookie header semantics exactly: non-cookie headers from the previous `#res` still override the new response; `content-type` from the previous response must still be skipped so the new response's content-type wins.
3. Cookie ordering: previously-set (middleware/context) cookies first, then the new response's cookies, matching `#newResponse`'s context-then-argument ordering.
4. Avoid introducing duplicate identical cookie strings. Important: when a handler returns a normal `c.text()`/`c.json()` response, `#newResponse` already copied `#preparedHeaders` cookies into the Response; the compose layer then calls the setter with that Response. Do NOT duplicate those cookies. Only merge cookies that are not already present in the incoming response.
5. Do not merge non-cookie headers from `#preparedHeaders` when `#res` is undefined (keep Hono's existing "raw Response ignores context headers" behavior). Only cookies from `#preparedHeaders` may be merged in that path.
6. Keep the `_res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)` recreation before mutating headers (needed for immutable/proxied headers in existing tests).

TEST CHANGES in `src/context.test.ts` (describe('Context header')):
a) The existing test `'Should set cookie headers when re-assigning Response to `c.res`'` (around lines 430-445) currently asserts the buggy behavior: after assigning a response with cookie `foo3=bar3` over a `c.res` with `foo=bar` and `foo2=bar2`, it expects only the original two cookies. It MUST be updated so all three survive, in order `[...cookies, ...newCookies]`.
b) Add a regression test that models the reported scenario directly: set a cookie on `c.res` first, then assign a `new Response(...)` that has its own Set-Cookie header, and assert both cookies are present via `getSetCookie()` (assert exact array/order + both values). Name it clearly, e.g. 'Should keep both Set-Cookie headers when a new Response is assigned to c.res'.
c) Optionally add one more focused test proving a cookie set through `setCookie(c, ...)` before the response is materialized (prepared-headers path) also survives assignment of a raw Response with its own Set-Cookie. Keep it small.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Follow the file's existing style (prettier-ish formatting, no semicolons, single quotes).
- Do not change public types or unrelated behavior.
- Do not touch any other file.

VERIFY: run `pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts` from the repo root and report the exact Test Files/Tests summary. If it fails, diagnose and fix before reporting.

REPORT BACK: the final diff (git diff) for both files, the exact test command output summary, and a short explanation of how both cookies survive and how duplicate cookies are avoided.

## How it works

- **Both cookies survive:** The setter no longer deletes the incoming response's `set-cookie` values. Instead, it iterates `#res` headers only for non-cookie, non-`content-type` overrides (unchanged semantics), then calls `#mergeCookies` with the context/middleware cookies.
- **Ordering:** `#mergeCookies` seeds `mergedCookies` with the context cookies first, then appends only incoming cookies not already in that list, and finally rebuilds the response's `set-cookie` headers. So middleware/context cookies come first, handler cookies after — matching `#newResponse`'s context-then-argument ordering.
- **No duplicates:** Incoming cookies already present in the context set are skipped (`includes` check). This matters when a handler returns `c.text()`/`c.json()`: `#newResponse` already copied `#preparedHeaders`/`#res` cookies into that Response, so the merge is a no-op for those identical strings (verified by the existing `'Should set set-cookie header values if c.res is already defined'` test expecting exactly `a, b, c`).
- **Prepared-headers path:** When `#res` is undefined but `#preparedHeaders` exists, only its cookies are merged (prepended, deduped); non-cookie prepared headers are still ignored, preserving Hono's "raw Response ignores context headers" behavior.
- **Recreation preserved:** `_res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)` remains before any header mutation, so immutable/proxied headers are replaced by a mutable copy.

At runtime compose() can assign a non-Response truthy value (a Context, e.g. middleware `return next()`), and these compose paths exist in src/compose.test.ts. If `#preparedHeaders` or `#res` has headers/cookies, the setter would call `.headers` on a Context and throw.

Apply these changes in src/context.ts (keep tests as they are unless a change is needed):
1. Change the guard from `if (_res)` to `if (_res instanceof Response)`. Keep `this.#res = _res` and `this.finalized = true` outside the guard exactly as now, so non-Response assignment behavior is unchanged.
2. With the instanceof guard, the redundant nested `if (prevHeaders || cookies.length > 0)` wrapper is no longer needed. if (_res && typeof _res.headers?.has === 'function') {
```

part.text:
## Result

Fixed the `Context.res` Set-Cookie merge bug and added regression coverage. All changes are **unstaged**; nothing was added, staged, or committed.

### Root cause

Old setter behavior (`src/context.ts` pre-fix) dropped the incoming response's cookies:

```ts
const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')   // deletes the handler's cookies
for (const cookie of cookies) _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
```

So when middleware had already set a cookie on `c.res` and the handler returned `new Response(..., { headers: { 'Set-Cookie': ... } })`, only the middleware cookie survived.

### Fix — `src/context.ts:414-453`

- Detects a previous cookie source: materialized `#res` headers, or `#preparedHeaders` before the first assignment (`src/context.ts:419-423`).
- Computes only cookies **missing** from the incoming response, so both sets survive without duplicating cookies that `#newResponse` already copied (`src/context.ts:424-431`).
- Creates a fresh mutable `Response` before any header mutation, then merges missing context cookies first, incoming cookies after (`src/context.ts:433-448`). This is immutable/fetch-response safe.
- Preserves existing non-cookie semantics: prior `#res` headers still override, incoming `content-type` wins, and prepared non-cookie headers are not merged.
- Guards `getSetCookie()` behind `Headers.has('set-cookie')` for runtimes that lack it (`src/context.ts:423-427`).
- Guards against compose passing a truthy non-Response value (`src/context.ts:418`) and prevents stale prepared cookies from resurrecting after `c.res = undefined` (`src/context.ts:420-422`).

### Tests — `src/context.test.ts`

- Updated the previous test that encoded the buggy expectation: three cookies now survive in order (`src/context.test.ts:431-446`).
- Added regression tests:
  - middleware cookie + handler `Set-Cookie` both survive (`:448-456`)
  - `setCookie()` prepared before materialization also survives (`:458-466`)
  - immutable incoming headers are copied, never mutated (`:468-483`, `:504-517`)
  - no stale prepared-cookie resurrection (`:485-490`)
  - no duplicate cookies after `#newResponse` (`:492-496`)
  - prepared non-cookie headers are still not merged (`:498-502`)
- Strengthened the test helper to enforce immutability for `set`, `append`, and `delete` (`src/context.test.ts:5-18`).

### Verification

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts` | **1 file passed, 70 tests passed** |
| `pnpm exec vp test --run src/hono.test.ts src/compose.test.ts src/helper/cookie/index.test.ts` | **3 files passed, 287 tests passed** |
| `pnpm exec vp test --run src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.test.ts src/adapter/lambda-edge/handler.test.ts` | **2 files passed, 88 tests passed** |
| `pnpm exec vp fmt --check src/context.ts src/context.test.ts` | clean |
| `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |

Two independent code reviews were performed; the blocking compatibility issue (unconditional `getSetCookie()`), immutability path, stale prepared cookies, and test gaps were addressed.

@@ -11,7 +12,7 @@ const makeResponseHeaderImmutable = (res: Response) => {

+    expect(() => {

--- a/src/context.ts
+++ b/src/context.ts
@@ -412,20 +412,39 @@ export class Context<

   set res(_res: Response | undefined) {
-    if (this.#res && _res) {
-      _res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)
-      for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {
-        if (k === 'content-type') {
-          continue
+    // compose() can pass a truthy non-Response value (e.g. the Context returned by next()),

+    // and mutation below; the assignment itself still happens either way.
+    if (_res && typeof _res.headers?.has === 'function') {
+      const prevHeaders = this.#res?.headers
+      // `#preparedHeaders` is only a cookie source before the first assignment. After
+      // `c.res = undefined` (finalized), stale prepared cookies must not be resurrected.
+      const cookieSource = prevHeaders ?? (!this.finalized ? this.#preparedHeaders : undefined)
+      const contextCookies = cookieSource?.has('set-cookie') ? cookieSource.getSetCookie() : []

+          ? _res.headers.getSetCookie()
+          : []
+      const missingCookies =
+        existingCookies.length > 0
+          ? contextCookies.filter((cookie) => !existingCookies.includes(cookie))
+          : contextCookies
+
+      if (prevHeaders || missingCookies.length > 0) {
+        _res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)
+        if (prevHeaders) {
+          for (const [k, v] of prevHeaders.entries()) {
+            if (k === 'content-type' || k === 'set-cookie') {
+              continue
+            }
+            _res.headers.set(k, v)

-        if (k === 'set-cookie') {

+        if (missingCookies.length > 0) {
